issues.failure_explanation: By (14) the quantity (\partial_t\psi, w)_{J_T} is real, so \mathrm{Re}(\mi(\partial_t\psi,w)_{J_T}) = 0, not \int|\partial_s\psi|^2 e^{-s/T}. The real part actually yields 0 = \mu[\frac{1}{2T}\int|\psi|^2e^{-s/T} + \frac{1}{2e}|\psi(T)|^2], which gives nothing when \mu=0. Moreover, even the displayed (incorrect) identity does not imply \psi\equiv 0 when \mu<0, since the terms then have opposite signs; \mu\in\R is allowed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take the real part correctly to get \psi\equiv0 for \mu\neq0, and for \mu=0 take the imaginary part (\int|\partial_s\psi|^2e^{-s/T}=0 with \psi(0)=0); or simply invoke uniqueness for the linear ODE.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of uniqueness in Proposition 3.2 is invalid as written; the statement itself is true (explicit ODE solution) and nothing downstream depends on this proof.
issues.title: Uniqueness proof of Prop. 3.2 misidentifies the real part and ignores the sign of mu
issues.why_classification: Local, routine correction of a proof of a true auxiliary continuous-level statement with no dependents.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The symbol polynomial $q^{\mathbf{K}^p(\rho)}$ of the family $\{ \K_n^p(\rho) \}_n$ defined in \eqref{eq:21} is a reciprocal polynomial.

issues.failure_explanation: q^{B^p} is palindromic (z^{2p}q^{B}(1/z)=q^{B}) and q^{C^p} is anti-palindromic (z^{2p}q^{C}(1/z)=-q^{C}). Their combination q^{K}=\mi q^{B}-\rho q^{C} satisfies z^{2p}q^{K}(1/z)=\mi q^{B}+\rho q^{C}, which is not a scalar multiple of q^{K} for \rho\ne0; hence \xi root does not imply 1/\xi root. Explicitly for p=2, q^K=(z-1)G(z) with 24G(z)=(\rho'-4\mi)z^3+(11\rho'-12\mi)z^2+(11\rho'+12\mi)z+(\rho'+4\mi), whose coefficient ratios a_0/a_3\ne a_1/a_2, so G (hence q^K) is not reciprocal. What holds is self-inversiveness (roots closed under \xi\mapsto 1/\bar\xi, because B,C have real coefficients), which still gives type (\ell,2p-2\ell,\ell).

failure_location.quote: both $q^{\B^p}$ and $q^{\bC^p}$ are reciprocal polynomials, and from \eqref{eq:25}, it follows that $q^{\K^p(\rho)}$ is also a reciprocal polynomial for all $\rho \in \R$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 'reciprocal' by 'self-inversive/conjugate-reciprocal' (z^{2p}\overline{q^K}(1/z)=-q^K(z) using real coefficients of q^B,q^C), which yields the same root-count symmetry.
issues.overall_effect: The stated reciprocity property in Proposition 3.9 is false and its proof step is invalid; the consequence used later (equal numbers of roots inside/outside the unit circle) remains true via a corrected argument, so Theorem 3.13 survives.
issues.title: Symbol polynomial q^{K^p(rho)} is not reciprocal; the linear-combination inference is invalid
issues.why_classification: A short local replacement argument restores the needed conclusion; no result is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $ \{\A_n\}_n $ be a family of nonsingular Toeplitz band matrices as in \eqref{eq:22}.
Let $\{\A_n\}_{n}$ represent a family of nonsingular Toeplitz band matrices as in \eqref{eq:22}
For all $p \in \mathbb{N}$ with~$p \geq 1$, $h > 0$, and $\mu \in \R$, the variational formulation~\eqref{eq:10} admits a unique solution.

issues.failure_explanation: Both cited theorems require the Toeplitz family {A_n} to be nonsingular. Assumption 3.4 only covers the nearly Toeplitz matrices K_n^p(\rho). The paper claims applicability once the outer codiagonals are nonzero, but never verifies (or assumes) nonsingularity of the pure Toeplitz extensions, whose symbol has zeros on the unit circle so nonsingularity for every n is not automatic.

failure_location.quote: Theorem \ref{th:39} is applicable to $ \{\K_n^p(\rho)\}_n $, and to the family consisting of the extensions of the purely Toeplitz band parts of $ \K_n^p(\rho) $ to $ n \times n $ matrices, provided that we show the entries of the two outer codiagonals

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Extend Assumption 3.4 (or add an explicit hypothesis) to nonsingularity of the Toeplitz extension family, or supply an argument/citation that the cited conditioning results hold with only asymptotic nonsingularity.
issues.overall_effect: The chain Prop. 3.9 -> Theorem 3.13 applies Theorems 3.8/3.9 with an unverified hypothesis; Theorem 3.13 (and its use in Theorem 4.2) inherits the gap.
issues.title: Nonsingularity of the pure Toeplitz extension family, required by Theorems 3.8/3.9, is never established or assumed
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard hypothesis to an already assumption-based theorem is a local fix that preserves the stated conditional guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For~$\rho>0$ and~$p \in \mathbb{N}$, the function $K_p(\theta,\rho)$ has exactly 2 simple zeros
Combining Propositions \ref{prop:39} and \ref{prop:312}, we obtain the main result of the paper.
provided that we show the entries of the two outer codiagonals (the $(-p-1)^{\text{th}}$ and the $(p-1)^{\text{th}}$) of $\K_n^p(\rho)$ are nonzero for all $\rho>0$

issues.failure_explanation: The root count on the unit circle is only proved for \rho>0. For \rho<0 nothing is said (the eigenvalues \mu of \frac12\Delta+V are negative in the paper's own numerical example, so \rho=\mu h<0 is the relevant regime). For \rho=0, \theta=0 is a double zero of K_p (\partial_\theta K_p\to-\rho=0), so the 'two simple zeros' argument fails and Prop. 3.9 is applied outside what was shown.

failure_location.quote: Then, for all~$p \in \N$ and~$\rho \in \R$, the family of matrices~$\{\K_n^p(\rho)\}_n$ defined in~\eqref{eq:21} is weakly well-conditioned.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For \rho<0 use K_p(-\theta,\rho)=K_p(\theta,-\rho) (B_p even, C_p odd) to transfer the root count; for \rho=0 note q^{K}=\mi q^{B} has a double root at z=1 (still two unit-modulus zeros counted with multiplicity) or cite the known weakly well-conditioning of {B_n^p}.
issues.overall_effect: As written, unconditional stability is only supported for \rho>0; the cases \rho<0 and \rho=0 asserted in Theorem 3.13 are not covered by the given argument.
issues.title: Theorem 3.13 claims all rho in R but Proposition 3.12 only covers rho > 0
issues.why_classification: The missing cases follow by an immediate symmetry observation and a citation already used in the paper; the theorem's scope survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Moreover, Lemma \ref{lem:a1} implies that the corresponding family of Schur complements is weakly well-conditioned for all $\mu_s \in \R$.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma A.1 bounds \kappa(S) by \kappa(M) (full matrix controls Schur complement). The final step of the proof needs the reverse direction: from \kappa(S) polynomial in n (and \kappa(B) polynomial) deduce that the 2x2 block matrix of (30) is weakly well-conditioned. No such bound is stated or proved; the block-LU estimate \|M^{-1}\|\lesssim \|B^{-1}\|(1+\|C\|\|S^{-1}\|(1+\mu_w\|C\|\|B^{-1}\|)) is required and omitted.

failure_location.quote: Hence, the weakly well-conditioning of these Schur complements implies the stability of formulation~\eqref{eq:30} for all $p \in \mathbb{N}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the reverse estimate via the block factorization M=[[I,0],[-\mu_w CB^{-1},I]][[B,C],[0,S]], bounding \|M\| and \|M^{-1}\| by \|B\|,\|B^{-1}\|,\|C\|,\|S\|,\|S^{-1}\|, all polynomial in n.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem 4.2 (alternative stability proof for the wave-equation method, advertised in abstract/introduction) has an unjustified final inference; the conclusion is recoverable.
issues.title: Theorem 4.2 infers conditioning of the full block matrix from its Schur complement, the converse of what Lemma A.1 provides
issues.why_classification: A short standard block-matrix computation closes the gap without changing the statement.

issues.failure_explanation: With X=(\mi B)^{-1}C=QRQ^H, (35) factors as (\mi B\otimes I)(Q\otimes I)(I\otimes M+R\otimes A)(Q^H\otimes I)\Psi=F, so the correct steps are Y=((\mi B)^{-1}\otimes I)F, (I\otimes M+R\otimes A)Z=(Q^H\otimes I)Y, \Psi=(Q\otimes I)Z. Algorithm 1 instead solves (B\otimes I)Y=F (missing the factor \mi), uses the matrix R\otimes A+R^{-1}\otimes M, and sets \Psi=-(Q\otimes I)Z. Composing the steps shows the output solves (\mi C\otimes A-\mi BC^{-1}B\otimes M)\Psi=F, not (35); the formal cases A=0 and M=0 fail with different factors, so no single scalar correction repairs it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite steps 2, 4, 5 as the standard Bartels–Stewart reduction: solve (\mi B\otimes I)Y=F, solve (I\otimes M+R\otimes A)Z=(Q^H\otimes I)Y, set \Psi=(Q\otimes I)Z.
issues.overall_effect: The stated solver procedure does not compute the solution of (35); the theoretical results are unaffected, and the numerical results rely on the (external) code rather than the pseudocode.
issues.title: Algorithm 1 as written does not solve system (35)
